title: Pass the Controller: How Single Console Households Split 'GTA VI'
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI is 2026’s breakout entertainment event. By the numbers, it made roughly $3.79 billion in revenue at launch, outpacing the lifetime earnings for megahit films like Avatar, The Odyssey, and Avengers: Infinity War. PlayStation called it their biggest launch of all time with over 39 million players on the platform alone. It’s the center of the current cultural zeitgeist, whether it’s because of the game’s controversy, music, love story, cultural legacy, or its accolades.

Entire households are playing GTA VI with one slight hitch: unlike movies, TV shows, or even books you can read side by side, a single-player, 40+ hour experience is tough to enjoy when you live together.

title: All the Worst Government GTA Memes from Around the World
content:
Grand Theft Auto VI is a true monocultural event. Every news channel is covering it, anyone with a passing interest in video games is playing it, and it’s made almost $4 billion in less than a week. Desperate to connect with constituents, governments around the world have tried to capitalize on GTA’s popularity by releasing some of the worst AI-generated memes I’ve ever seen. The pictures of politicians in the hyper-real cartoon pink-tinted style of GTA 6 are so awful they even caused a minor political scandal in Scotland.

Let’s begin in the United States, where Vice President JD Vance, the White House, and several other government-run X accounts attempted to capture the cultural zeitgeist by quickly churning out AI-generated meme garbage. GTA has long been popular with Trump 2.0 officials. In March, the official X account of the White House published a compilation of strikes on Iranian targets overlaid with the “WASTED” game over screen from GTA.

title: The Birds Are Listening: Scientists Used Seabirds to Track Hidden Ships
content:
In what sounds like an avian riff on The Wire, scientists equipped seabirds with audio recorders in order to listen in on their interactions with fishing vessels across the world’s oceans, according to a study published on Wednesday in Science Advances.

The approach exposed a large number of so-called “unseen” vessels that did not have their location trackers switched on. Many vessels are required to continuously signal their location using the Automatic Identification System (AIS), which openly broadcasts a ship’s location, similar to flight tracking. But AIS can be disabled for legitimate reasons—such as evading pirates—or with more nefarious motivations, such as concealment of illegal fishing activities. 

The new study was not designed to interrogate why any particular vessel switched off its AIS tracker. However, the discovery that seabirds are regularly interacting with unseen ships can shed light on broader efforts to monitor commercial fisheries, while also revealing new insights about seabird behavior, especially their risk of becoming “bycatch” when they are fatally trapped in fishing gear.

title: I Listened to ‘Sandstorm’ Through a Sex Toy
content:
You don’t really realize how much downtime there is in the song “Sandstorm” by Darude until you’re waiting for the bass to drop while it’s playing inside your vagina. 

In August 2025, I got an email with the subject line “‘Airpods for your @ss’ raises nearly half a million in Kickstarter campaign.” I get a lot of zany pitches for products that don’t exist yet, and a lot of pitches for products that do exist but perhaps should not. This one was for a device called the Groove Thing, a sex toy that turns music into vibration patterns. But the pitch didn’t include the phrase “sex toy” at all. Instead, it’s called an “internal music player.” 

I asked for a unit to review, expecting this to be purely conceptual. But they had one, and offered to send it. “The prototype functions very similarly to the final product but we do want to stress it’s a garage built prototype,” the rep for Groove Thing told me. I thought for a moment about putting something “garage built” and connected to a wall outlet into an orifice and passed. While others were braver, I decided to wait until the version they planned to send to customers in the fall was ready.

title: Treasury CIO Is Vibe Coding a ‘Civilization’ Clone During Treasury Department Hack
content:
As the Treasury Department dealt with the fallout of a hack that took down some of its services, its Chief Information Officer was pushing updates to Legatum, his vibe coded Civilization clone.

Sam Corcos is the cofounder of the A16z-backed glucose monitoring health startup called Levels; he became the Treasury Department’s Chief Information Officer as a DOGE hire near the beginning of Trump’s second term, and has been a leading AI evangelist within the administration since. Corcos’s department is in charge of cybersecurity for the Treasury Department, and so it is possibly concerning that while the Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN) is dealing with a “cybersecurity incident” that has taken a critical bank compliance reporting panel down, he has been actively pushing balance patches, new theme music for the Aztec faction, and critical tweaks to the in-game player assistance tooltips for Legatum, his vibe-coded “turn-based strategy game in the tradition of Civilization VI.”

content:

The patent is the latest signal of the AI video endgame: endless highly specific, customized content that is automatically generated based on the wealth of data companies and advertisers collect about you.

title: University of Michigan Mailer Promises Its Data Center Isn’t Really a Data Center
content:
Over the past month, the University of Michigan sent postcards and pamphlets to people in Michigan telling them its new data center is “NOT a commercial data center” and is, instead, a “research computing center.”

According to one of the postcards viewed by 404 Media, the University’s data center will “advance breakthrough research in medicine, clean energy, cybersecurity, and engineering,” and "accelerate discoveries like new drug therapies and cancer treatments that improve people’s lives.” The University's postcard also promised to create 300 “high-quality union jobs during development” and “preserve approximately 80% of the 124-acre property as green space.”

One of U of M’s mailers said the building will not operate as a commercial data center. “This facility will not support streaming, entertainment, social media, or e-commerce,” it said. It also said the facility will not “burden the local community with the cost of its energy or water use, drain resources from the local community or raise utility rates,” or “create smoke, odors, or significant noise.”

title: University Approves Nuclear Weapons Data Center, Township Vows to Fight On
content:
Last week, the University of Michigan’s board of regents approved the construction of a $1.25 billion data center that will power American nuclear weapons research. The regents voted 7 - 1 in a public meeting on November 19 to move forward with the project despite widespread opposition from faculty, staff, and the residents of Ypsilanti Township, Michigan where the data center will operate. A few hours after the vote, the leaders and citizens of the Township gathered to discuss how to stop it.

U of M and Los Alamos National Laboratories (LANL) first announced plans to build what the University then called an “AI research facility” in 2024. U of M now calls the project a “research computing center” and, if all goes to its plan, construction will begin on a 125,000 square foot facility in late 2027. The data center could expand to “no more than 300,000 square feet,” according to a U of M blog post.

During the regent’s meeting, faculty, staff, and members of the community shared their thoughts on the data center’s construction.

title: “I’m not going to remove the repository”
content:
There is a hacking tool called ARTEX that is causing havoc around the world. It lets a hacker plug in their LLM of choice, and ARTEX will then spin up a bunch of AI subagents focused on different aspects of hacking, such as scoping out a target or stealing data. This tool can complete an entire hack of a target in just a few hours. The original author of ARTEX took down the tool in October after it became clear that bad people were using it. But, as I write below, ARTEX is free. Several people are still distributing it on GitHub. I spoke to them about it, asked them why, and for their thoughts about requests to take the tool down. 

And as I’m writing this, NVIDIA just said it has reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO, and Board Director. Hahahahahahahahahha.

title: ‘The Code Is Already Copied Everywhere’: The AI Hacking Tool Causing Havoc Around the World
content: ARTEX, an open source framework that makes it easy for AI agents to hack companies at superspeed, is causing havoc. People using the tool appear to include Chinese hackers breaking into targets for espionage, and financially-motivated hackers too. Earlier this month, the FBI published a warning to potential targets, and said hackers using ARTEX have targeted government, healthcare, telecommunications, legal, defense, financial services, and semiconductor sectors globally.

title: Scientists Discover New and Horrible Eagle-Based Way Our Ancestors Died
content:
Welcome back to the Abstract! Here are the studies this week that dive-bombed our ancestors, brightened the sky, recalled an old tune, and got hosed by marine mucus.

First, scientists discover that eagles are hunting large baboons, hinting that early human relatives once sated ancient avian appetites. Then: star-on-star contact, a musical memory lane, and the secrets of cetacean snot. 

As always, for more of my work, check out my book First Contact: The Story of Our Obsession with Aliens, or subscribe to my personal newsletter The BeX Files.

Hobaiter, Catherine et al. “Signs of Eagle Predation on a 22-kg Adult Primate.” American Journal of Biological Anthropology.

Death came from the sky for early humans, according to a new study that suggests giant eagles preyed on our ancestors far more recently than was previously known.
